summary:
MARS - GEO is an interactive 3D and 2D topographic explorer designed as a survival and navigation guide for future crewed missions to Mars. Using web technologies (Three.js and raster rendering in HTML5 Canvas) alongside NASA cartographic references (Mars Trek, MOLA altimetry data, and the USGS Planetary Geologic Mapping Program), the platform allows users to explore a three-dimensional Martian globe featuring 10 key scientific regions, including volcanoes, canyons, and rover landing sites.

To address surface mobility and safety challenges, selecting any location causes the system to transition into a 2D topographic map featuring contour lines, hillshading, and an interactive cross-section tool (Section A → B) that calculates real-time slopes, distances, and elevation changes. This tool is essential because it allows astronauts to assess terrain risks and plot safe routes before and during extravehicular activities (EVAs).
details:
What does it do and how does it work?MARS - GEO is an interactive 3D and 2D geospatial exploration platform designed to assist in astronaut navigation and survival on Mars. The system operates in two integrated phases: first, an interactive three-dimensional Martian globe that allows users to visualize the entire planet and select 10 key scientific regions (such as rover craters, volcanoes, and valleys); second, clicking on any location smoothly transitions the platform into a detailed 2D topographic map featuring hillshading, contour lines, and an interactive cross-section profile tool (Section A → B) that calculates terrain elevations, distances, and slopes in real time.

What benefits does it offer and what is its expected impact? The project provides a critical tool for planning extravehicular activities (EVAs), enabling the crew to identify geological hazards, avoid dangerous rock formations, and plot safe scientific routes. Its expected impact lies in substantially increasing the safety and efficiency of astronauts in hostile planetary environments, optimizing scientific and operational decision-making on Martian terrain.

What tools, programming languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Languages and Technologies: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (ES6+).
  • Libraries and 3D Engines: Three.js (for rendering and animating the 3D Martian globe and asteroids), Tailwind CSS (for designing the user interface with a retro/space aesthetic).
  • NASA/USGS Data Sources and Cartography: MOLA altimetry data, images from the official Perseverance and Curiosity galleries, USGS geological guides, and references from official portals such as Mars Trek (JPL).

In what way is your project creative? The creativity of the project lies in precisely combining immersive exploration in a 3D environment with the technical rigor of 2D topographic maps and real-time elevation profiles. Furthermore, it integrates a unique visual identity inspired by the original aesthetic of NASA space missions and Martian rover instrumentation.

What factors did your team consider?

  • Crew safety: Prioritizing the assessment of topographic risks (steep slopes and obstacles) to prevent accidents during spacewalks.
  • Scientific accuracy: Basing coordinates, elevations, and locations on real data collected by NASA and USGS missions.
  • Accessibility and performance: Developing an interactive, lightweight, and fluid web interface that runs directly in the browser without requiring complex installations of heavy software.
